question: Should OpenClaw accept a scheduled live agent-role eval workflow that hydrates provider/Codex secrets and bootstraps local Ollama, or should this PR be split to deterministic contracts only?
rationale: The code defects are repairable, but recurring secret-bearing automation and hidden CLI eval surface are maintainer policy and security-boundary choices rather than purely mechanical fixes.

options.title: Split deterministic contracts first
options.body: Land or review the deterministic harness/contract subset separately and keep the secret-bearing live workflow out until it is pinned, isolated, and proven.

options.title: Accept live workflow after hardening
options.body: Keep the full direction only after the workflow input, config/model semantics, action/image pinning, and proof blockers are fixed.

options.title: Replace the draft branch
options.body: Close or pause this unmergeable draft in favor of a narrower maintainer-owned replacement if the contributor cannot repair and prove it.

recommendation.title: Split deterministic contracts first
recommendation.body: Land or review the deterministic harness/contract subset separately and keep the secret-bearing live workflow out until it is pinned, isolated, and proven.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans agent-command behavior and maintainer ownership of live automation; Peter is the clearest adjacent owner from current agent-command history.
